name: House Ways and Means
verdict: The House committee that writes Medicare’s payment rules and the tax exemption every nonprofit hospital lives on. In January it changes hands, and 15 of its 45 members are gone, including both leaders of its Health Subcommittee.
verdictSource: Jurisdiction: House Rule X, clause 1(t), and the Health Subcommittee jurisdiction statement at waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/. Change of control: NBC News projected Democratic control of the House on the night of November 3, 2026, and AP called it early November 4. Departures: see the leaving table; Health Subcommittee chairman Vern Buchanan and ranking member Lloyd Doggett both retired.

plainEnglish.heading: What this committee does, in plain English
plainEnglish.intro: Every tax bill starts in the House, and every one starts here. Ways and Means writes the revenue code, Social Security and the House side of Medicare. On health care, it decides what Medicare pays and who pays no tax at all.

points.title: It writes Medicare’s rules for the House.
points.body: What Medicare pays a hospital and a physician, and why the hospital gets more for the same visit. Medicare Part A is its alone; Part B it shares with Energy and Commerce.

points.title: It writes the tax code.
points.body: Who pays tax and who does not. That includes the exemption nonprofit hospitals hold, the bonds that finance their towers, and the premium tax credits that buy coverage.

points.title: Medicaid is mostly next door.
points.body: Medicaid’s federal rules, including the provider taxes and directed payments that flow to hospital systems, are written by Energy and Commerce. Ways and Means reaches Medicaid where it touches Medicare or the tax code.

plainEnglish.source: House Rule X, clause 1(t), Rules of the House of Representatives, 119th Congress (H.Res. 5, adopted January 3, 2025): revenue measures generally; tax exempt foundations and charitable trusts; national social security except health programs supported from general revenues rather than payroll deductions. Clause 1(f)(3) gives Energy and Commerce health and health facilities except health care supported by payroll deductions: Medicare Part A is payroll-funded, Part B runs on general revenue and premiums and is shared in practice (Health Subcommittee jurisdiction statement, waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/; Rules of the Committee on Ways and Means, 119th Congress). Article I, Section 7 of the Constitution: all bills for raising revenue originate in the House. Chairman-designate Neal, post-election news conference as reported by masslive, November 4, 2026: “taxes, tariffs, Social Security, Medicare, the tax side of Medicaid.”

items.title: Medicare
items.body: What hospitals and physicians are paid under Part A and, with Energy and Commerce, Part B. That includes the higher rate a hospital gets for the same service in a building it owns.
items.note: Social Security Act, Title XVIII; House Rule X, clause 1(t)(9)

items.title: The tax exemption
items.body: Whether nonprofit hospitals keep their federal tax exemption, and what they must report and show for it.
items.note: Internal Revenue Code §501(c)(3) and §501(r); House Rule X, clause 1(t)(3) and (8)

items.title: Tax-exempt bonds
items.body: The cheap borrowing that finances hospital towers and acquisitions.

items.title: Health tax credits and accounts
items.body: The premium tax credits that buy marketplace coverage, and the health savings account rules the 2025 law widened.
items.note: Internal Revenue Code §36B and §223; Public Law 119-21, sections 71301 to 71308

whoRuns.heading: Who runs it in 2027
whoRuns.subtitle: Democrats won the House on November 3
whoRuns.source: NBC News, projection the night of November 3, 2026 (article updated November 4): Democrats win control of the House of Representatives, about 255 seats; AP called the House early November 4. Chair and ranking member are expected: the 120th Congress organizes in January 2027. Neal was elected chairman in January 2019 and led the committee through the 116th and 117th Congresses (neal.house.gov/biography); Smith was selected to chair in January 2023 (waysandmeans.house.gov/about/the-chairman/).

people.label: Expected chairman
people.name: Richard Neal
people.line: D-Massachusetts · chaired Ways and Means 2019 to 2023
people.text: Has named the expired ACA premium tax credits, Medicare cuts he says endanger Massachusetts hospitals, Social Security hearings and tariffs as his first priorities.
people.source: masslive (Jim Kinney, TNS) as published by CPA Practice Advisor, November 5, 2026: Neal “poised to do the job for the second time”; early priorities “restoring tax credits from the Affordable Care Act, reversing trillions of dollars in Medicare cuts that endanger Massachusetts hospitals and holding hearings on the future of Social Security”; “I would be willing to test him immediately on the tariff issue, as well.”

people.label: Expected ranking member
people.name: Jason Smith
people.text: Moves from the gavel to the minority with a thinner bench. 9 of his 25 Republican colleagues on the committee will not return.
people.source: waysandmeans.house.gov/about/the-chairman/: selected to chair in January 2023. Deloitte Tax News & Views, November 4, 2026: Smith expected to become ranking member in the 120th Congress; the formal choice is made in January. Leaving table below: 8 of the 25 other Republicans on the 119th Congress roster.

leaving.heading: Who is leaving
leaving.intro: Both leaders of the Health Subcommittee retired. So did the Budget Committee chairman. Eight members lost an election, and two left for a Senate seat and a governor’s mansion.
leaving.introSource: Health Subcommittee: chairman Vern Buchanan (Clerk of the House member data, leadership “Chair” on WM02) and ranking member Lloyd Doggett (doggett.house.gov/about). Budget chairman: Jodey Arrington (Clerk member data, BU00 leadership “Chair”). Lost an election: Schweikert and Feenstra (governor primaries), Larson (House primary), Fitzpatrick, Carey, Max Miller, Murphy and Gomez (general). Other office: Hern (Senate), Plaskett (governor of the Virgin Islands). Murphy conceded NC-03 on November 11 (Carolina Journal, unofficial State Board of Elections results). Thompson (CA-04) was not called as of November 12.

rows.name: Vern Buchanan
rows.source: Ballotpedia News, January 28, 2026: Buchanan announced January 27, 2026 that he would not seek reelection to FL-16 after 20 years. Health Subcommittee chairman: Clerk of the House member data (WM02, leadership “Chair”).

rows.name: Jodey Arrington
rows.loss: Chairman of the House Budget Committee. Sat on the Trade and Tax Subcommittees.
rows.source: Ballotpedia News, November 12, 2025: Arrington announced November 11, 2025 that he would not seek reelection to TX-19. Budget chairman: Clerk of the House member data (BU00, leadership “Chair”). Subcommittees: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: David Schweikert
rows.why: Ran for governor; lost the primary
rows.source: Fox News, July 21, 2026: AP called the Arizona Republican primary for governor for Rep. Andy Biggs; Schweikert had 17% of the vote, more than 50 points behind, with just under half the vote counted. Oversight chairman: Clerk of the House member data (WM06, leadership “Chair”).

rows.name: Brian Fitzpatrick
rows.loss: Health Subcommittee member. Seat won by Democrat Bob Harvie.
rows.source: NBC10 Philadelphia results page, updated 1:00 a.m. November 4, 2026: Harvie 52.7% (188,087) to Fitzpatrick 47.3% (168,531) in PA-01 at 98.5% counted; NBC News projected the race. Health Subcommittee: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: Randy Feenstra
rows.why: Ran for governor; lost the primary
rows.loss: Sat on the Social Security, Work and Welfare and Tax Subcommittees.
rows.source: Iowa Public Radio, June 2, 2026 primary results: Feenstra lost the Republican primary for governor to Zach Lahn, 37.8% to 37.0%, and conceded that night. Subcommittees: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: Mike Carey
rows.loss: Seat won by Democrat Don Leonard.
rows.source: WOSU, November 3, 2026 (wosu.org, "Democrat Don Leonard unseats Republican U.S. Rep. Mike Carey in stunning upset"): the AP projected Leonard the winner of OH-15; unofficial Ohio Secretary of State returns showed Leonard 52% to Carey 45% with 85% of precincts reporting.

rows.name: Max Miller
rows.loss: Seat won by Democrat Brian Poindexter.
rows.source: Ashland Source, November 4, 2026: Poindexter 54.93% (180,614) to Miller 45.07% (148,177) in OH-07, final unofficial Ohio Secretary of State totals.

rows.name: Greg Murphy
rows.loss: Health Subcommittee member. Seat won by Democrat Raymond Smith by 293 votes.
rows.source: Carolina Journal, November 11, 2026: Smith 118,488 (49.43%) to Murphy 118,195 (49.31%) in NC-03, unofficial State Board of Elections results after provisional and cured absentee ballots; Murphy conceded November 11.

rows.name: Kevin Hern
rows.loss: Health Subcommittee member. Takes the Oklahoma seat Markwayne Mullin vacated.
rows.source: AP race call, 9:36 p.m. EST November 3, 2026, as reported by KTAR News and OKC Fox: Hern defeated Democrat N’Kiyla Jasmine Thomas for the U.S. Senate seat Markwayne Mullin vacated. Health Subcommittee: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: Lloyd Doggett
rows.loss: Ranking member of the Health Subcommittee. Did not run after Texas redrew his district; the new seat went to Democrat Greg Casar.
rows.source: KUT, November 3, 2026: AP called the redrawn TX-37 for Greg Casar over Republican Lauren Peña; Doggett did not run after courts upheld the new Texas map (retirement pledge reported by Ballotpedia News, August 25, 2025). Health Subcommittee ranking member: doggett.house.gov/about.

rows.name: Danny Davis
rows.loss: Health Subcommittee member. Seat won by Democrat La Shawn Ford.
rows.source: Roll Call, July 31, 2025: Davis announced he would not seek a 16th term and endorsed La Shawn Ford; NBC Chicago live results, November 4, 2026: Ford won IL-07, 89.2% to 10.8%, over Chad Koppie. Health Subcommittee: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: Dwight Evans
rows.loss: Health Subcommittee member. Seat won by Democrat Chris Rabb.
rows.source: evans.house.gov release, June 30, 2025: Evans announced he would not seek reelection and would serve the full term ending January 3, 2027; WTOP (Associated Press), November 2026, "Democrat Chris Rabb wins election to U.S. House in Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District": Rabb won PA-03 over independent Dennis Mahoney. Health Subcommittee: waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/.

rows.name: John Larson
rows.loss: Lost to former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin, 53.5% to 34.7% when AP called the race.
rows.source: CT News Junkie, August 11, 2026 (ctnewsjunkie.com, "Bronin Wins 1st Congressional District Primary"): Bronin 53.5% to Larson 34.7% in unofficial results of the CT-01 Democratic primary; the AP called the race for Bronin that night.

rows.name: Jimmy Gomez
rows.loss: Lost an all-Democratic general election to Angela Gonzales-Torres.
rows.source: Jewish Insider, November 4, 2026, with NBC Los Angeles results: Gonzales-Torres 61.9% to Gomez 38.1% in CA-34 with 92.3% counted, NBC projection.

rows.name: Stacey Plaskett
rows.loss: The first woman elected governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands.
rows.source: TheGrio, November 3, 2026: Plaskett and running mate Milton Potter elected with 62.8%, the first woman to hold the office. The Green Papers, Virgin Islands 2026: the delegate seat was open because the incumbent ran for governor.

docket.heading: What is on the docket
docket.subtitle: The fights this committee will decide in 2027

items.title: The 2027 Medicare physician cut
items.body: Physicians take a 2.3% Medicare pay cut on January 1 because the one-year 2.5% raise in the 2025 law expires. A budget-neutrality fix cleared this committee 44 to 0 in May. An inflation update has 69 cosponsors and no markup.
items.status: IN PLAY · Cut takes effect January 1
items.source: CMS CY2027 Physician Fee Schedule final rule fact sheet, November 4, 2026: conversion factor $32.63 for non-qualifying participants, down from $33.40 (2.31%); the 2.5% increase for 2026 under Public Law 119-21, section 71202, expires. H.R. 8163 (Murphy), Provider Reimbursement Stability Act, ordered reported 44-0 at the May 21, 2026 markup (waysandmeans.house.gov markup page). H.R. 9693 (Joyce), Patients First Act, annual update of MEI minus one point, 69 cosponsors as of November 5, 2026 (AMA), referred to Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means, no markup.

items.title: The nonprofit hospital tax exemption
items.body: A bill making big hospitals disclose their 340B program revenue cleared the committee 25 to 15 in July and never reached the floor. It dies with this Congress. The incoming chairman names hospitals as something to protect, not to examine.
items.status: STALLED · Dies in January unless the House votes
items.source: H.R. 9504 (Murphy), Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act, ordered reported 25-15 on July 1, 2026 as amended by a Smith substitute (Votes of the Committee, waysandmeans.house.gov; Polsinelli in The National Law Review, June 4, 2026, on the committee’s discussion draft: expanded Form 990 Schedule H reporting for 501(r) hospitals, including 340B program revenue; AAMC Washington Highlights, July 2, 2026, on the reported bill; the bill does not change the 501(r) requirements themselves); House floor action NOT FOUND as of November 8, 2026. H.R. 3019 (Spartz), Holding Nonprofit Hospitals Accountable Act, community benefit equal to 100% of tax exemptions, in committee with no action. Neal priorities: masslive via CPA Practice Advisor, November 5, 2026 (“Medicare cuts that endanger Massachusetts hospitals”).

items.title: Site-neutral payment
items.body: Medicare still pays a hospital more than an independent office for the same visit. CMS is closing the gap one service at a time by rule: drug administration in 2026, imaging in 2027. A bill in this committee to narrow the loophole has no cosponsors and no hearing.
items.status: IN PLAY · Moving by rule, not by law
items.source: CMS CY2027 OPPS final rule (CMS-1850-F) fact sheet, November 4, 2026: imaging without contrast at excepted off-campus departments paid at the physician fee schedule equivalent rate from January 1, 2027, rural sole community hospitals exempt, CMS estimate $260 million in 2027; drug administration policy from the CY2026 rule continues. Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, section 6225: off-campus departments bill under their own NPI from January 1, 2028 (American Action Forum, January 29, 2026). H.R. 3023 (Spartz), Preventing Hospital Overbilling of Medicare Act, referred to Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means April 24, 2025, no cosponsors on govinfo, no action.

items.title: Physician-owned hospitals
items.body: A member of this committee wrote the bill to repeal the 2010 ban on new physician-owned hospitals. It has sat in committee since June 2025 without a hearing.
items.source: H.R. 4002 (Van Duyne, R-Texas, a Ways and Means member), Patient Access to Higher Quality Health Care Act of 2025, introduced June 12, 2025, repeals section 6001 and section 10601 of the Affordable Care Act and section 1106 of the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act; referred to Energy and Commerce and, in addition, Ways and Means (govinfo BILLS-119hr4002ih); committee action NOT FOUND as of November 8, 2026. H.R. 2191 (Griffith), Physician-Led and Rural Access to Quality Care Act, rural exception, 22 cosponsors as of May 29, 2025 (AMA).

items.title: The 340B drug payment cut
items.body: From January 1, Medicare pays hospitals 28% below average sales price for drugs bought through the 340B program. CMS made the $4.35 billion cut by rule. Hospitals want Congress to undo it. The committee has not scheduled a vote.
items.source: CMS CY2027 OPPS final rule (CMS-1850-F) fact sheet, November 4, 2026: 340B-acquired drugs paid at ASP minus 28% in CY2027 (proposed minus 33.4%), CMS estimate $4.35 billion less in Medicare drug payments and $1.1 billion less in beneficiary cost sharing, budget neutral through higher non-drug payments; remedy offset rises from 0.5% to 2% a year until $7.8 billion is recovered, estimated CY2031. AHA statement, November 4, 2026. No committee action identified as of November 8, 2026.

items.title: The ACA premium tax credits
items.body: The enhanced credits expired December 31, 2025. The House passed a three-year extension after a discharge petition; it is not law. The incoming chairman lists restoring them first among his priorities.
items.source: Deloitte Tax News & Views, November 4, 2026: enhanced ACA premium tax credit expired December 31, 2025; House-passed three-year extension, H.R. 1834, advanced via discharge petition. masslive via CPA Practice Advisor, November 5, 2026: Neal’s early priorities begin with “restoring tax credits from the Affordable Care Act.” Presidential term runs to January 2029.

staff.heading: Work for a member of this committee?
staff.text: Every health system in your member’s district and state, with its subsidies, reserves, executive pay and offshore holdings, sourced to the filing. Ready for a hearing.
